text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/donor-design-astra.md <<'EOF'
# Individual donor parsing design sketch

Ground and sketch are complete. Agree, implementation, and scrap are outside this runner's assignment. No repository files changed.

## Consumer outcome

Cleaning should retain `Lord (Michael) Farmer` verbatim and additionally expose title `lord` and person name `michael farmer`. The reconstructed normalized person form is `lord michael farmer`. This is evidence preparation, not an identity merge or a claim about given names and surnames. Existing organization, matching, and loaded display behavior remain stable.

## Evidence in this checkout

`domain/models/funder_name.rs` owns parallel candidate representations for all funder roles. `from_name` has no donor-kind input. Its `person_core` already tokenizes parentheses away and strips leading titles, so `Lord (Michael) Farmer` already yields `michael farmer` there. The missing information is separately retained titles and a less destructive normalized person representation.

`domain/models/declaration_cleaning.rs::observe_roles` creates features for donor, payer, and ultimate payer. `FunderObservation` flattens those features into serialized rows. `outbound/declaration_cleaning.rs::funders_schema` explicitly lists Arrow fields; a Rust-only field addition does not establish the artifact contract.

`domain/models/declaration_resolution/input.rs::Observation` consumes `name_normalized`, `organisation_core`, and aliases, not `person_core`. Exact-name matching, indexes, checks, and attribution depend on `name_normalized`. `outbound/declaration_resolution.rs::read_table` requires every field in the current `funders_schema`, so new fields make old cleaned artifacts require regeneration, even when resolution ignores the added values.

`outbound/declaration_loading.rs::canonical_funders` selects canonical names and aliases from `name_raw`. Consequently additive cleaning features will not change the public canonical display spelling. If the user's intended outcome is visible public names changing, explicitly include a separately justified loading-policy change; do not silently mutate raw evidence to achieve it.

## Preferred usage and types

The public constructor remains `FunderNameFeatures::from_name(Some("Lord (Michael) Farmer"))`.

Its serialized additions are `person_titles: ["lord"]` and `person_name_normalized: "michael farmer"`. Existing `name_raw`, `name_normalized`, and `parenthetical_text` retain their current values. Untitled usable names have an empty title list and a normalized person candidate. Missing/withheld names have an empty list and null person candidate.

Use one domain `PersonTitle` enum with variants covering the existing title vocabulary. Serialization uses lowercase spellings. Implement a single boundary parser from normalized title tokens and an exhaustive canonical-spelling match only if needed. `Prof` and `Professor` can be separate variants to retain the existing lexical distinction. Likewise `Rev`/`Reverend`, `Rt`/`Hon`. Do not add a second title string array. Preserve source order and repeated titles. No inferred gender, rank, first name, or surname fields.

A private `ParsedPersonName` owns the title vector and title-free normalized remainder, and derives the legacy core through existing punctuation tokenization. `FunderNameFeatures` receives its results. This removes the old title-strip allowlist rather than maintaining two independent rules. Keep the parser internal; the current single public constructor is sufficient.

Invariants are owned by `ParsedPersonName`: consume only a leading run of recognized whole title tokens, optionally followed by periods; preserve apostrophes, hyphens, accents, and internal punctuation in the normalized remainder; never recognize a title in the middle of a name. `person_core` stays semantically backward compatible by applying the existing punctuation tokenizer to the same remainder. Verify punctuation variants against legacy tokenization before replacing it.

## Parenthesis rule

The new person candidate may unwrap one balanced, nonnested group immediately after a recognized leading title, with nonempty simple name-like content and a nonempty name-like suffix. It must retain the enclosed words. Reject unbalanced or nested groups, numbers, conjunctions, and explicit trading-as markers from this rewrite. Leave all other parentheses unchanged in the candidate. Existing raw evidence and parenthetical extraction never change.

This rule is intentionally syntactic. `Lord (Holdings) Smith` is still ambiguous without entity-kind evidence, so the person representation remains explicitly a candidate. It must not overwrite generic normalized names or organization features. For known individuals, downstream code could choose that candidate later under an explicit matching/display contract. Avoid global removal of brackets in `normalize`, which would change `BJD (GB) Limited` and identity matching.

One possible simpler implementation preserves all parentheses in `person_name_normalized` and relies on `person_core` for bracket-free matching. That does not provide the requested normalized spelling directly, so it is insufficient unless the request is explicitly narrowed.

## Structurally distinct alternative

Introduce `NameEvidence { raw, status, candidates: NameCandidates }` where candidates is an enum distinguishing Person, Organisation, and Unknown. Parse donor kind at the cleaning boundary; Person holds typed titles and normalized name. Resolution consumes the same typed candidate instead of loose fields, and serialization emits a versioned tagged structure.

This alternative makes entity-specific behavior explicit and can safely drive individual canonical display names. It requires a new interpretation for untyped payer and ultimate-payer names, unknown kinds, and the existing deliberately parallel candidate features. It also spreads changes across cleaning, Arrow serialization, resolution constructors/tests, artifact validation, and loading. That cost is not justified for adding evidence fields. It risks discarding useful parallel features when the source's entity kind is incomplete or wrong.

## Synthesis decision

Prefer the additive representation with an internal parser and one title enum. It satisfies separate titles and normalized personal spelling without changing generic identity evidence. Model the Domain shaped the choice to centralize title vocabulary and parsing in a typed owner rather than adding a second stripping helper. Keep organization features untouched and treat this as parsing evidence, not entity classification.

## Producer and consumer work

1. Add enum and internal parsed representation in `funder_name.rs`; derive the two new serialized fields and existing `person_core` from one title parse.
2. Preserve the existing `from_name` call in `observe_roles`; cover all roles because the cleaning abstraction is role-neutral.
3. Add a nonnullable Utf8-list `person_titles` and nullable Utf8 `person_name_normalized` to `funders_schema`.
4. Resolution's Observation can continue ignoring added fields. Verify the reader accepts newly written rows and that old artifacts receive the existing regeneration error. State this artifact compatibility effect.
5. Loading continues using raw spellings and existing aliases. No SQL changes, no migration, no identity rule change, and no financial effects.
6. Document the added cleaned-artifact columns wherever the current fields are described. Search repository scripts and fixtures for schema assumptions, not only Rust struct construction.

## Verification contract

Unit cases cover Mr/Mrs/Lord/Dame, title chains, dotted titles, untitled names, title-like words in the middle, accented and hyphenated names, apostrophes, absent/withheld input, title-only input, and preservation of raw text. Define title-only output explicitly rather than accidentally converting an existing empty core to a new missing-value meaning.

Parenthesis cases cover `Lord (Michael) Farmer`, an untitled company with parentheses, organization acronyms and trading-as text, nested/unbalanced/empty groups, and suffix parentheses. Assert every preexisting organization field is unchanged for organization examples.

An integration test should replay realistic captured donor JSON, clean it, publish with the production storage writer, read `funders.parquet`, and assert the actual list/null/text values and preserved raw spelling. Deserialize the same artifact through `read_resolution_input` to catch schema and serde mismatches. An empty-funders table test confirms the complete schema exists even with no records. Unit serialization alone is insufficient because Arrow's explicit schema is the real integration point.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));

Saved [design sketch](/tmp/donor-design-astra.md).

Recommend one `PersonTitle` enum and internal parser producing separate titles and normalized person-name candidates while preserving raw and organization evidence. Include actual Parquet round-trip verification.

Two integration constraints matter:

- Loading selects display names from `name_raw`; additive features alone will not change public spelling.
- Adding required Arrow fields means existing cleaned artifacts need regeneration.

No repository changes.
